items: Escribe un arco claro con inicio, transición y cierre.
Asigna un movimiento de cámara a cada momento en lugar de acumular instrucciones.

Mantén los diálogos breves y vincula cada frase a una acción o expresión concreta.

faqs.a: Muestra cómo Seedance 2.5 convierte texto, imágenes, referencias multimodales y vídeo fuente en resultados cinematográficos más largos con audio generado opcional.

faqs.q: ¿Cuánto duran las escenas que se muestran?
faqs.a: Los ejemplos del tren y del andén duran 24 segundos. Seedance 2.5 permite escenas de 4 a 30 segundos; la galería incluye otras duraciones.

faqs.q: ¿Cómo se escribe el prompt de una escena más larga?
faqs.a: Primero define el concepto, asigna acciones y cámara a momentos concretos y después indica las restricciones de continuidad y seguridad que deben mantenerse.

faqs.q: ¿Puedo generar con Seedance 2.5 desde esta página?
faqs.a: La generación con Seedance 2.5 está disponible para los usuarios de MaxVideoAI; el precio se calcula y se muestra antes de cada render.

Draft nativo es un flujo de Seedance 2.5 en dos generaciones: crea una vista previa a 480p, revisa movimiento y composición y solicita el final a 1080p desde ese Draft completado. Draft y final son generaciones con presupuestos separados. Un render normal a 480p no es un Draft nativo; el final hereda prompt, duración, encuadre, audio y referencias del Draft completado.

tabs.label: Concepto
tabs.title: Define el arco de la escena
tabs.description: Establece quién aparece, qué cambia y dónde debe terminar la escena.
tabs.copy:
Sujeto y entorno:
[Quién aparece, dónde está y cuáles son sus detalles visuales distintivos]

Cambio narrativo:
[Qué ocurre desde el momento inicial hasta el último]

Encuadre final:
[La acción, expresión o composición final]

Lenguaje visual:
[Luz, paleta, textura y carácter de la lente]

tabs.label: Cronología
tabs.title: Dirige momentos narrativos pautados
tabs.description: Distribuye las acciones y el movimiento de cámara durante toda la escena.
tabs.copy:
0-6 segundos:
[Composición inicial + primera acción + movimiento de cámara]

6-14 segundos:
[Desarrollo + reacción + transición de cámara]

14-22 segundos:
[Revelación principal o momento de interpretación + encuadre]

22-30 segundos:
[Resolución + posición final de cámara]

Dirección de audio:
[Ambiente, diálogo breve y sonidos ligados a las acciones]

tabs.label: Restricciones
tabs.title: Protege la continuidad y la claridad
tabs.description: Indica qué elementos no pueden desviarse mientras avanza la escena.
tabs.copy:
Anclas de continuidad:
[Vestuario, objetos, ubicación, luz y dirección en pantalla]

Reglas físicas:
[Contacto, peso, velocidad y reacciones del entorno]

Reglas de interpretación:
[Miradas, gestos, expresión facial y ritmo del diálogo]

Evitar:
[Cortes no deseados, sujetos duplicados, cambios bruscos de cámara y artefactos visuales]

tabNotes.body: El concepto fija un único cambio narrativo legible para toda la escena.
La cronología asigna una acción y un movimiento de cámara a cada momento.
Las restricciones repiten solo los detalles que deben permanecer estables.

globalPrinciples: Describe un arco completo antes de añadir detalles de cada toma.
Usa tramos temporales para ordenar las acciones en lugar de pedirlo todo a la vez.
Mantén un lenguaje de cámara deliberado y físicamente compatible con la escena.
Vincula gestos, expresiones y diálogos breves a momentos narrativos visibles.
engineWhy: Planificar una escena más larga deja espacio suficiente para planteamiento, desarrollo y cierre.
La dirección pautada facilita evaluar la cámara y la interpretación momento a momento.
Las reglas físicas explícitas ayudan a conservar movimiento y reacciones creíbles durante la secuencia.

demo.title: Demostración cronológica de Seedance 2.5
demo.prompt:
Cinematic 24-second landscape video, 16:9. A woman in her early thirties waits alone on a quiet European railway platform at sunrise. She wears a timeless camel coat and places a weathered brown suitcase on the ground. Maintain her appearance, clothing, the suitcase design, and the platform architecture consistently throughout the video.

0-4 seconds: medium-low camera angle. She opens the suitcase. A warm golden light immediately illuminates her face from inside. The camera begins one slow, continuous forward dolly toward the open suitcase.

4-17 seconds: inside the suitcase, a realistic miniature coastal city unfolds and comes alive in one continuous action: compact buildings rise, a small train moves along the coast, tiny cars begin moving, harbor water ripples, and waves reach the shore. The camera continues the same smooth forward movement and descends into the city. Preserve believable scale, geometry, gravity, and natural motion. No sudden transformation, no cut, no change of visual style.

17-24 seconds: the camera gently rises into a wide view showing the complete living coastal city still contained inside the open suitcase. The woman remains visible beyond it at giant scale, watching in quiet amazement. Golden sunrise, subtle sea mist, realistic materials, cinematic contrast, premium feature-film photography. End on a stable, readable composition with no text, no logo, and no watermark.
notes: Abre el ejemplo para ver el prompt original y los ajustes. Las plantillas anteriores son puntos de partida que puedes adaptar.
En el siguiente intento, cambia una acción visible o indicación de cámara. Mira el resultado completo antes de complicar el plano.

shotPlans.prompt: SEEDANCE | TEXT TO VIDEO | SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE | 15s | HORIZONTAL 16:9 SCENE AND LOCATION A hidden volcanic spring canyon deep in a Pacific Northwest pine forest on a bright summer day. A narrow deep gorge with high walls of dark gray basalt columns, tan and rust streaks, bright green moss and ferns. At the bottom is a crystal-clear natural spring pool: turquoise shallow edges, deep sapphire center, honeycomb volcanic rock, mossy boulders and two pale submerged logs. Two white waterfalls, one at the far back and one spilling from the right cliff. Tall pine trees line the rim under a clear blue sky. The same canyon layout throughout. THE JUMPER First-person view only. Tanned bare feet, lightly hairy shins and loose navy-blue swim shorts with a mustard-yellow hibiscus pattern. Bare hands and forearms naturally enter frame. No face, shoes or gloves. CAMERA AND REALISM Forehead-mounted action-camera POV with a natural ultra-wide lens. Breathing micro-jitter, head bob, fast exposure shifts between sky and shade, water droplets after immersion, wind buffeting during the fall. Authentic action-camera footage. The drop is about 35 meters. Continuous real-time motion, gravity and water behaviour; keep the same limbs and shorts. 0-2s | THE EDGE AND TAKEOFF Look steeply down at the turquoise pool from the basalt ledge: feet at the bottom of frame and a pink-and-white inflatable tube already floating far below. One sharp breath and a quick "Let's go!" Two quick steps and a decisive push off the edge. The pool and the two waterfalls remain in view as the cliff edge falls away. 2-5s | THE FALL Fast uninterrupted descent. Arms briefly spread at frame edges, then tuck in; legs straighten for a feet-first pencil dive. Basalt and moss rush upward past the lens, right-side waterfall spray catches the sun, wind builds and the camera shakes naturally. The pool and pink tube grow quickly without changing position. One breathless "Wooo!" No pause or slow motion. 5-6s | IMPACT The water fills frame. Feet-first entry: one hard splash, then white bubbles swallow the lens. Audio immediately becomes muffled underwater. 6-10s | UNDERWATER AND ASCENT The bubbles clear into transparent blue water, sun shafts, the same pale logs and basalt bottom. One strong arm pull enters frame, then upward kicks towards the bright surface; bubbles stream past. Keep the ascent fast and purposeful. 10-12s | SURFACE BREAK Burst through the surface. Droplets slide down the lens, wind and waterfall sound return clearly, one hand grabs the pink-and-white tube beside the camera. 12-15s | REWARD Bob on the turquoise water holding the tube. Tilt up to show the towering basalt cliff, the tiny takeoff ledge, pines and right-side waterfall. A real breath, then natural spoken English: "That was insane!" Finish on the cliff view with the water gently bobbing. AUDIO AND CONTINUITY Wind, breathing, waterfall roar, one clear impact splash, bubbles underwater, water movement on resurfacing and the three brief English reactions. One continuous upbeat chill electronic instrumental beneath the real sounds: build through the fall, muffled underwater, then restore clarity with a small beat drop on surfacing. No narration or sung lyrics. One continuous first-person shot, no third-person cut, hovering, extra slow motion, morphing cliffs, changing water colour, extra limbs, titles, subtitles, borders or watermarks.

items.prompt:
30-second live-action POP COMEDY commercial, 16:9, set in present-day Southern California. A mischievous giant DESKTOP MOUSE CURSOR edits the real world around a young woman. Nine short, connected comic beats with a beginning, escalating playful chaos and a cute final punchline. Preserve the playful abundance: ice cream, duplication, a fluffy dog, candy-colored paint, an eraser, a rescue and a surprise hairstyle. Bright, youthful, funny and charming.

LOOK AND PLACE
A sunny Santa Monica neighborhood shopping street: broad American concrete sidewalks, low pastel-pink and mint storefronts, a small ice-cream shop with a striped awning, palm trees, a turquoise bench, a parked compact white delivery van, a coral-brick side alley. Real California street proportions and contemporary American summer styling. Midday sunshine, clear cobalt sky, vivid candy colors, clean whites, crisp faces, colorful details and real tactile materials. Light, buoyant commercial photography with kinetic tracking and comic reaction cuts. No muted sepia palette, brown grading, bleak backstreet or solemn luxury-ad mood. No readable brands or lettering.

CHARACTER CONTINUITY
One fictional 23-year-old woman, called MAYA only for prompt clarity: lively expressive face, shoulder-length dark-brown hair in a high ponytail, small silver hoop earrings, coral-pink fitted short-sleeve T-shirt, white wide-leg jeans, clean white-and-pink sneakers. Natural young-adult American streetwear. Keep her face, body, clothes and accessories identical in every shot. Only her hairstyle changes near the end. She reacts with surprise, mischievous amusement and comic exasperation, never terror.
One small fluffy white bichon with round dark eyes, a tiny pink bandana and a happy wagging tail, initially on a slack coral leash held by a young adult dog walker in a mint sweatshirt. Its later enlarged form is exactly the same adorable dog, with proportional paws and soft detailed curls, never monstrous.

THE CURSOR MUST LOOK LIKE A REAL COMPUTER POINTER
Use the unmistakable classic desktop mouse-pointer silhouette: a broad asymmetric white arrowhead pointing diagonally UPPER LEFT, an inward notch on the lower-right edge and a short diagonal tail. Thin black outline, matte white face, shallow solid thickness. It is NOT an upright street-direction arrow, not a spear, not a signpost. It floats at waist-to-head height, normally about 1.2 meters tall, with accurate shadows, perspective and occlusion in the street. It has an impish personality expressed by quick tilts and bouncy motion, but no face, eyes or limbs.
EVERY click is visible and audible: the pointer tip jabs forward a few centimeters, a crisp mechanical mouse CLICK is clearly heard, and the edit happens immediately in the same shot. A black-and-white dotted selection rectangle and small square transform handles briefly make the operation legible. These are physical graphic shapes embedded in the scene, not a full-screen software interface. For the paint and eraser beats the cursor snaps briefly into those recognizable tool icons, then returns to the same diagonal mouse pointer.

SOUND IS ESSENTIAL
Deliver a clearly audible soundtrack from the first second: original upbeat playful electro-funk/pop instrumental around 116 BPM, bouncy bass, handclaps, tight drums and little sparkling synth accents. Mix sound effects forward so each mouse click and comic action remains unmistakable above the music. Add real footsteps, street ambience, ice-cream pops, a soft elastic enlargement, happy dog barks, paint swoosh, eraser squeaks, rubber-toy squeaks, a splash shake and a final springy BOING. Briefly cut the music before the final hairstyle gag, then bring back a playful ending sting. No dialogue, voice-over, singing or subtitles. Let expressions and synchronized sounds tell the story.

SHOT 1 | 0.0–3.5 s | A DELIGHTFUL LITTLE FAVOR
Medium close shot, slight upward camera tilt following the action. Maya sits on the turquoise bench about to lick a single scoop of strawberry-pink ice cream. Within the first second the classic diagonal mouse cursor swoops into frame and selects the scoop with a tiny dotted rectangle. Four fast visible clicks, each with a distinct CLICK-POP, duplicate the scoop upward into a wobbly five-scoop tower. Each scoop physically rests on the one below. Glossy creamy texture, little melting drips catching the sun. Her eyes follow the growing tower; she breaks into a delighted grin and gives the cursor an appreciative nod. Immediate cute surprise, no static introduction.

SHOT 2 | 3.5–7.0 s | NOW IT GETS CHEEKY
Same bench and screen direction. The cursor pivots toward Maya; CLICK: a dotted rectangle encloses her and the bench. Her grin turns into a suspicious side-eye. Keeping her ice cream upright, she carefully scoots sideways out of the rectangle. CLICK-THUMP: the empty bench duplicates beside the original. The bump makes the upper scoops tumble onto the pavement with soft SPLATS. She looks at her sad remaining scoop, then at the cursor: an unmistakable “really?” look. She leaves the cone on the bench and springs into a playful run toward screen right. Pan with her.

SHOT 3 | 7.0–11.0 s | THE CUTEST ACCIDENT
Lateral tracking shot. Maya nimbly runs around the small bichon and its walker. The cursor's selection misses Maya and lands on the fluffy dog. CLICK: corner handles pull outward, and the dog scales smoothly and proportionally to small-pony size. Elastic BOOP, then one happy low WOOF. Its paws stay grounded; its fur and pink bandana remain identical. The walker lets go of the slack leash in surprised delight, safely staying clear. The giant dog wags its tail enthusiastically and focuses on the cursor as if it were an irresistible toy. Maya does a quick comic double take while continuing right. Make the dog endearing and huggable.

SHOT 4 | 11.0–14.0 s | COLOR FLOOD
Maya ducks alongside the parked white delivery van. The cursor instantly becomes a paint-bucket icon, tips toward the van and CLICKS. A vivid glossy LILAC color races across the van's painted panels with a satisfying liquid SWOOSH. The windows, wheels and headlights remain unchanged. Maya hops clear just before the color reaches where she was leaning, checks her spotless white jeans, gives a tiny relieved smile and keeps moving. Rich purple against pink storefronts and blue sky; clean, instantaneous visual comedy.

SHOT 5 | 14.0–17.5 s | THE ERASER
Tracking alongside the coral-brick wall. The cursor snaps into a chunky white eraser and sweeps toward Maya; she ducks beneath it in one smooth motion. SQUEAK-SQUEAK: the eraser rubs a square of brick into a flat gray-and-white transparency checkerboard, still in perspective on the wall. Maya stops for a fraction of a second, pokes the flat checkerboard with one finger, raises an eyebrow, then darts away as the eraser comes back. The checkerboard is a solid flat surface, not a glowing portal. Keep this curious reaction light and quick.

SHOT 6 | 17.5–22.0 s | THE FLUFFY RESCUE
Maya reaches the end of the colorful side alley and turns. At the entrance, the cursor becomes the diagonal arrow again, briefly scales larger and prepares a selection. Before it can click Maya, the huge happy bichon bounds in from behind it and gently catches the cursor's tail like a rubber dog toy. WOOF, then a clear toy SQUEAK. Cut to a side view of the whole playful action: the dog settles onto its paws, cursor reduced to its usual size, gently chewing it while its tail thumps the sidewalk. Maya exhales and laughs silently with relief. No biting a person, no aggression, no harm.

SHOT 7 | 22.0–25.0 s | FALSE VICTORY
Medium two-shot, warm faces and fluffy texture. Maya scratches the dog's chin, delighted with her rescuer. The dog opens its mouth to pant; the soggy cursor slips onto the pavement. Behind Maya, it bobs back into the air and shakes droplets off with a little PRRR-SPLASH, straightening back into its pristine diagonal pointer shape. She is busy cuddling the dog and does not notice. The audience sees the mischievous comeback.

SHOT 8 | 25.0–27.5 s | ONE LAST CLICK
The music stops for a comic beat. A loud, clean CLICK: a small dotted selection frames ONLY Maya's hair. POP-BOING: her ponytail instantly becomes a huge fluffy BUBBLEGUM-PINK curly hairstyle, a round cloud of springy, individual curls. Keep her exact face, clothing and earrings. She freezes, slowly pats the top of the new hair; it bounces twice with a soft spring sound. Her expression is deadpan disbelief, not distress. The cursor gives an innocent little tilt.

SHOT 9 | 27.5–30.0 s | THE LOOK
Close group composition with the entire pink hairstyle visible, Maya in the middle, the diagonal mouse cursor beside her and the giant bichon's face entering from below. Maya side-eyes the cursor. The adorable dog notices the round bouncy pink hair, tilts its head, wags faster and lowers its front paws into a playful bow. Maya's eyes slide toward the dog: “don't even think about it.” The cursor innocently rocks twice to two little electronic BLIPS. End on this funny three-way reaction with a bright musical button and tail THUMP-THUMP. The dog does not jump on Maya. Hold the expression for the final half-second.

DIRECTING PRIORITIES
Each edit must show target selection, a visible click, a sharp audible click and an immediate result. Keep the cheerful pop energy throughout, with enough reaction time for every joke. Camera tracking carries Maya consistently left to right until the alley; normal clean cuts maintain geography. Physical effects are crisp and harmless, with shadows and material detail. Preserve natural live-action actors and a realistic fluffy dog rather than plastic 3D characters. No text, logos, watermark, unrelated landscape cutaways, beach, doorway or spoken slogan. The final brand title will be added later; generate only the complete colorful comedy with sound.

highlights.title: Create. Modify. Extend.
highlights.body: Elige tu punto de partida: crear, modificar un plano o continuar la historia.

specialty.title: Encuentra la toma. Después, termínala.
specialty.intro: Draft nativo es un flujo de Seedance 2.5 en dos generaciones: crea una vista previa a 480p, revisa movimiento y composición y solicita el final a 1080p desde ese Draft completado.

steps.label: Draft 480p
steps.body: Explora la dirección con una vista previa.

steps.label: Final 1080p
steps.body: Conserva la configuración del Draft y solicita el final.

specialty.note: Esquema del flujo. Draft y final son generaciones con presupuestos separados. Un render normal a 480p no es un Draft nativo; el final hereda prompt, duración, encuadre, audio y referencias del Draft completado. Draft está disponible en Create, Modify y Extend; la fuente y las referencias permanecen vinculadas al flujo de finalización.

capabilities.title: Un modelo. Tres formas de construir una película.
capabilities.intro: Elige tu punto de partida: crear, modificar un plano o continuar la historia.

items.label: Create
items.title: Parte de una idea. O trae tus referencias.
items.body: Escribe una escena, anima una imagen inicial o guía el resultado con imágenes, vídeos y audio de referencia. Asigna una función a cada referencia: personaje, movimiento, cámara, entorno o sonido.
uses: Primer + último fotograma: guía el inicio y el final de un plano creado desde imágenes.
Referencia de movimiento: toma un gesto o recorrido de cámara y describe el personaje y el entorno deseados.
Multimodal: combina hasta 30 imágenes, 10 vídeos y 10 referencias de audio.
items.note: De 4 a 30 segundos, o duración automática. Los vídeos de referencia comparten 30 segundos; las referencias de audio tienen otros 30 segundos en total.

items.label: Modify
items.title: Conserva el plano. Cambia lo que importa.
items.body: Trae un clip y describe la edición. Cambia un personaje o su vestuario, sustituye el fondo, modifica la luz y la atmósfera, o añade y elimina elementos. Explica también qué debe mantenerse.
uses: Personaje y estilo: cambia la apariencia, la ropa o un objeto.
Entorno y atmósfera: transforma el lugar, la iluminación, el tiempo o el tratamiento visual.
Sonido y referencias: guía cambios de audio y explica la edición con imágenes, vídeos o sonidos.
items.note: Modify sigue el encuadre y la duración de la fuente. Regenera el plano: revisa rostros, manos, movimiento y continuidad. Los ajustes disponibles aparecen en Create.

items.label: Extend
items.title: Dale otro momento a la escena.
items.body: Continúa después de un clip, crea una entrada antes de él o describe una transición entre planos. Explica la acción en el corte, así como la cámara y el sonido que deben continuar.
uses: Después: termina una acción, revela el entorno o mantén una reacción.
Antes: establece una llegada o una entrada al plano original.
Entre: usa varios clips originales para guiar una transición.
items.note: Hasta 10 clips originales, 30 segundos en total. Solicita un nuevo segmento de 4–30 segundos con el formato de la fuente, para revisar y montar con tu material.

controls.title: Completa la dirección
controls.body: Añade diálogo, ambiente y efectos, o desactiva el audio generado. Usa referencias de imagen y audio para fijar los detalles. Elige duración, formato y resolución en Create; revisa el presupuesto antes de cada generación.
